meta.source: Bambu Lab Wiki + CRASH Space Makerspace Reference
meta.notes: Seed database for OrcaSlicer Printer Help System. Covers P1S/P1P HMS codes. Community contributions welcome.

severity_levels.fatal: Print stopped. Immediate action required. Power off if instructed.
severity_levels.warning: Print may continue but issue should be addressed soon.

errors.name: Heatbed temperature abnormal: heater short circuit
errors.description: The heatbed temperature is abnormal. The heater may have a short circuit.
fix_steps: Stop the print immediately and power off the printer.
Allow the bed to fully cool before inspecting.
Check the bed heater cable and connector under the bed and at the base for damage or loose connections.
Inspect for scorch marks, burns, or melted insulation on the cable.
Do not resume use if visual damage is present. Contact Bambu Lab support.

errors.name: Heatbed temperature abnormal: sensor short circuit
errors.description: The heatbed temperature is abnormal. The thermistor sensor may have a short circuit.
fix_steps: Pause the print and let the bed cool to room temperature.
Power off the printer.
Check the bed thermistor cable connector under the bed for a loose or partially unplugged connection.
Inspect the cable for cuts, pinches, or burns.
If the error returns after reseating, the thermistor or cable likely needs replacement. Contact support.

errors.name: Heatbed temperature abnormal: sensor open circuit
errors.description: The heatbed temperature is abnormal. The thermistor sensor may have an open circuit (broken wire).
fix_steps: Stop the print and allow the bed to cool.
Power off the printer.
Reseat the bed thermistor connector on both ends.
Check the cable for a break or complete disconnection.
If the issue persists, the thermistor or wiring harness requires replacement.

errors.name: Heatbed over temperature
errors.description: The heatbed temperature is abnormal. The heater is over temperature.
fix_steps: Power off the printer immediately.
Allow the bed to cool completely.
Check that the correct build plate type and material profile are selected in Bambu Studio.
Verify the target temperature set in the print profile is within normal range for the material.
If the bed repeatedly overheats at normal target temperatures, the AC board or thermal management may be faulty. Contact support.

errors.name: Heatbed heating anomaly: heating module may be broken
errors.description: An abnormality occurred during the heating process of the heatbed. The heating modules may be broken.
fix_steps: Power off the printer and disconnect from power.
Allow full cooling before any inspection.
Check that nothing conductive is under the plate or on the contacts.
Reseat the build plate and verify it is the correct plate type.
Do not continue printing until the bed and wiring have been inspected. Contact Bambu support.

errors.name: Nozzle temperature abnormal: heater short circuit
errors.description: The nozzle temperature is abnormal. The heater may have a short circuit.
fix_steps: Stop the print immediately. Do not touch the nozzle.
Power off the printer and disconnect from power.
After cooling, open the toolhead front cover.
Reseat the hotend heater cable connection.
Check the ceramic heater resistance with a multimeter (should be ~10Ω at room temperature).
If damaged or reading is incorrect, replace the hotend assembly. Contact support for guidance.

errors.name: Nozzle temperature abnormal: heater open circuit
errors.description: The nozzle temperature is abnormal. The heater may have an open circuit.
fix_steps: Stop the print and allow the hotend to cool.
Open the toolhead front cover and reseat the heater cable connector.
If the connector looks undamaged, measure heater resistance (~10Ω expected at room temp).
A reading of infinity indicates an open/broken heater wire.
Replace the hotend assembly or contact support.

errors.name: Nozzle over temperature
errors.description: The nozzle temperature is abnormal. The heater is over temperature.
fix_steps: Stop the print immediately. The nozzle is very hot, do not touch it.
Power off the printer.
After cooling, reseat the NTC sensor cable on the toolhead.
Check that the silicone sock is present and intact. Replace it if missing or damaged.
The quickest diagnostic is to try a known-good replacement hotend.
If the issue persists with a new hotend, the toolhead board may need replacement.

errors.name: Nozzle temperature abnormal: NTC sensor short circuit
errors.description: The nozzle temperature is abnormal. The thermistor (NTC) sensor may have a short circuit.
fix_steps: Stop the print and power off the printer.
After cooling, open the toolhead front cover.
Reseat the NTC cable connector.
Measure NTC resistance with a multimeter (~100 kΩ at room temperature).
A reading near zero indicates a short; replace the hotend assembly.

errors.name: Nozzle temperature abnormal: NTC sensor open circuit
errors.description: The nozzle temperature is abnormal. The thermistor (NTC) sensor may have an open circuit.
fix_steps: Stop the print and power off the printer.
After cooling, open the toolhead front cover and reseat the NTC cable. Sometimes reseating multiple times is needed.
Check for a broken wire or damaged connector on the NTC.
Measure NTC resistance (~100 kΩ expected at room temp); infinity reading indicates an open circuit.
Check that the silicone sock is intact.
Replace the hotend assembly if the sensor or wire is broken.

errors.name: Part cooling fan too slow or stopped
errors.description: The speed of the part cooling fan is too slow or it has stopped.
fix_steps: Pause the print and visually check the part cooling fan on the toolhead for obstructions.
Remove any filament strands or debris caught in the fan blades.
With the printer off, spin the fan blades by hand; they should spin freely.
Check the fan cable connector on the toolhead board.
If the fan does not spin at all during printing, it likely needs replacement.

errors.name: Hotend fan too slow or stopped
errors.description: The speed of the hotend cooling fan is too slow or has stopped. This can lead to heat creep and clogs.
fix_steps: Stop the print immediately. A stopped hotend fan can cause heat creep and a serious clog.
Power off the printer and let everything cool.
Check the hotend fan for debris or filament wrapped around the blades.
Spin the fan by hand to check for binding.
Check the fan cable connection on the toolhead board.
Replace the hotend fan if it does not spin freely or fails to start.

errors.name: Motor-A open circuit
errors.description: Motor-A has an open circuit. There may be a loose connection or the motor may have failed.
fix_steps: Power off the printer.
Check the motor cable connector for the affected axis (Motor-A is typically the X-axis extruder motor on P1 series).
Reseat the connector firmly on both the motor and the board.
Inspect the cable for visible damage.
If the error persists after reseating, the motor or its driver may have failed. Contact support.

errors.name: Motor-A short circuit
errors.description: Motor-A has a short circuit. The motor may have failed.
fix_steps: Power off the printer immediately.
Do not attempt to run the motor again until inspected.
Check the motor cable for damage, melting, or pinching.
Measure motor coil resistance if you have a multimeter.
Contact Bambu Lab support. Motor replacement will likely be needed.

errors.name: Motor-A resistance abnormal
errors.description: The resistance of Motor-A is abnormal. The motor may have failed.
fix_steps: Power off the printer.
Reseat the motor cable connector on both ends.
Check for bent or pushed-back pins on the connector.
If the connector looks good and the error returns, the motor likely needs replacement.
Submit a support ticket and include printer logs.

errors.name: Build plate not properly placed
errors.description: The build plate may not be properly placed. The nozzle could not detect the plate correctly during probing.
fix_steps: Remove the build plate and clean both the plate and the magnetic bed surface.
Reinstall the plate ensuring all corners are flat and it is not crooked.
Make sure you are using a Bambu-compatible plate; third-party plates with different structures can trigger this error.
Run a bed leveling calibration before the next print.
If using a textured or smooth PEI sheet, confirm the plate type is set correctly in the slicer.

errors.name: Heatbed homing abnormal: possible bed bulge
errors.description: Heatbed homing is abnormal. There may be a bulge or obstruction on the bed surface.
fix_steps: Remove the build plate and inspect the magnetic bed and plate for warping or debris.
Check for any dried filament blobs on the nozzle that could cause false contact.
Clean the nozzle tip and the bed surface.
Reinstall the plate and run a full calibration.
If the plate is visibly warped, try a replacement plate.

errors.name: Accelerometer data unavailable
errors.description: The accelerometer data is unavailable. This affects vibration compensation and resonance calibration.
fix_steps: Restart the printer and attempt calibration again.
Check for firmware updates; this can be a known firmware issue in some versions.
If the error persists, the IMU/accelerometer on the toolhead board may be faulty.
Contact support if restarting and updating firmware does not resolve it.

errors.name: X-axis resonance mode low
errors.description: The 1st order mechanical resonance mode of the X-axis is lower than expected, indicating a mechanical issue.
fix_steps: Check X-axis belt tension; it should be firm but not excessively tight.
Inspect the X-axis rail and linear rod for debris, dried grease, or damage.
Clean and re-lubricate the linear rods with a small amount of appropriate lubricant.
Check that the toolhead moves smoothly by hand along the full X range.
Re-run vibration compensation calibration after addressing mechanical issues.

errors.name: Toolhead front cover fell off
errors.description: The front cover of the toolhead has fallen off or is not properly attached.
fix_steps: Pause or stop the print.
Locate the front cover and check it for cracks or broken clips.
Snap the cover back into place firmly; all four corners should click in.
Inspect the area for any loose parts that may have been hit during printing.
If the cover clips are broken, a replacement cover should be sourced before continuing unattended prints.

errors.name: Serial port data transmission abnormal
errors.description: Data transmission over the serial port is abnormal. The software system may be faulty.
fix_steps: Restart the printer and try the print again.
Check for a firmware update; communication errors are sometimes resolved in newer firmware.
If the error recurs consistently, there may be a hardware issue with the main control board.
Contact support and provide your printer logs.

errors.name: System voltage unstable: power failure protection triggered
errors.description: The system voltage is unstable, triggering the power failure protection function.
fix_steps: Check that the power cable is fully seated at both the printer and the wall outlet.
Try a different power outlet or power strip.
Check that the printer is not on an overloaded circuit shared with other high-draw devices.
Inspect the power cable for damage.
If the voltage issue persists on a known-good outlet, the power supply unit may be failing. Contact support.

errors.name: Heatbed force sensor sensitivity too high
errors.description: The sensitivity of heatbed force sensor 1/2/3 is too high, which may affect bed leveling accuracy.
fix_steps: Remove everything from the build plate surface.
Make sure no cables or objects are pressing against the underside of the bed.
Run a full auto-calibration from the printer menu.
If the error persists, the force sensor or its mounting may need inspection by support.

errors.name: Heatbed force sensor sensitivity too low
errors.description: The sensitivity of heatbed force sensor 1/2/3 is too low, which may cause bed leveling failures.
fix_steps: Clean any debris from around the bed mounting points and sensor area.
Ensure the build plate is seated flat and not wedged on an edge.
Run a full auto-calibration.
If this occurs after a physical impact to the printer, inspect the sensor mounting.
Contact support if the error is persistent.

errors.name: AMS filament speed and length error: odometry may be faulty
errors.description: AMS filament speed and length error. The filament odometry may be faulty.
fix_steps: Check for tangles or heavy drag in the AMS path and buffer tube.
With the AMS door open, try feeding filament by hand to confirm it moves freely.
Power-cycle both the printer and AMS.
If the error repeats across multiple prints, the AMS hall-effect odometry sensor may be failing. Open a support ticket.

errors.name: AMS communication error
errors.description: Communication error between the printer and AMS hub.
fix_steps: Power off both the printer and AMS.
Reseat the AMS communication cable on both ends.
Avoid sharp bends or heavy objects on the cable route.
Turn the printer back on and wait for the AMS to fully initialize before starting a print.
If multiple AMS units are daisy-chained, test with only one connected to isolate the fault.

errors.name: AMS internal sensor error
errors.description: General AMS internal sensor fault.
fix_steps: Power-cycle the printer and AMS and wait for all AMS LEDs to show normal status.
Remove all spools and check for loose filament fragments inside the AMS channels.
Run a short multi-color test print to verify all slots can load and unload.
If the error repeats or specific slots consistently fail, contact support with the exact code.

errors.name: AMS disabled but filament still loaded
errors.description: The AMS has been disabled for this print, but filament is still loaded in an AMS slot.
fix_steps: On the printer screen or in Bambu Studio, either re-enable AMS for this job or unload the active AMS slot.
If you want to print from the rear external spool holder, unload all AMS filament for that toolhead first.
Restart the print after resolving the conflict.

errors.name: Filament still loaded after AMS disabled
errors.description: Filament remains loaded from the AMS path after the AMS was disabled.
fix_steps: Use the unload function in the printer menu to pull the filament out of the AMS path.
Confirm the printer is set to use the external spool or rear holder for the intended tool.
Restart the job after unloading.

errors.name: AMS filament run out
errors.description: AMS filament has run out in the currently active slot.
fix_steps: Load a new spool into the AMS slot shown on screen.
Cut the filament tip cleanly at a 45-degree angle and feed it into the AMS until it is grabbed.
Press Retry on the printer screen.
If you do not want to continue with AMS, unload and switch the job to the rear external spool holder.

errors.name: AMS filament cutter error: failed to cut
errors.description: Failed to cut the filament at the AMS cutter.
fix_steps: Open the AMS side cover and visually inspect the cutter area for debris or jammed filament.
Clean out any filament chips and verify the cutter blade can move freely by hand (follow AMS safety precautions).
Close the cover and press Retry.
If the error continues after clearing, the cutter assembly may need replacement. Contact support.

errors.name: AMS cutter stuck
errors.description: The AMS filament cutter is stuck and cannot complete its stroke.
fix_steps: Gently pull out and reseat the cutter handle as described in the AMS maintenance guide.
Look for filament wedged around the blade and carefully remove it.
Press Retry and monitor the first few tool changes to confirm normal operation.
If the cutter repeatedly jams, inspect for wear and order a replacement cutter assembly.

errors.name: Failed to pull filament from extruder: possible clog
errors.description: Failed to pull filament out of the extruder. Possible clog or broken filament in the path.
fix_steps: Use the Unload or Cold Pull procedure to clear the hotend and extruder path.
Inspect the PTFE tube between the extruder and AMS buffer for a broken filament piece.
If a broken piece is present, push it through gently from the AMS side.
Once the path is clear, reload filament and resume the print.

errors.name: AMS slot motor slipped
errors.description: AMS slot motor slipped. The extrusion wheel may be worn, filament may be too thin, or there is high resistance in the feed path.
fix_steps: Check that the filament diameter is consistent and not soft or ovalized.
Ensure the spool rotates freely and the filament is not tangled or rubbing against the AMS case.
Try a different filament to rule out material issues.
If the same slot keeps slipping with normal filament, the AMS slot drive wheel or motor may need service.

errors.name: AMS slot empty or filament broken in AMS
errors.description: The selected AMS slot is empty, or the filament has broken inside the AMS.
fix_steps: Confirm that a spool is actually installed in the indicated slot.
Open the AMS and check whether filament has snapped inside; remove any loose piece.
Reload filament cleanly and press Retry or restart the job.

errors.name: AMS RFID read error
errors.description: The RFID tag on the AMS spool cannot be read or is damaged.
fix_steps: The filament can still be used; you simply lose the auto-profile from RFID.
Manually select the material type and profile in Bambu Studio or on the printer screen.
If RFID errors appear across multiple slots, the AMS RFID board may require service.
Try cleaning the RFID contacts on the spool hub with a dry cloth.

errors.name: Failed to pull filament back from toolhead to AMS
errors.description: Failed to retract the filament from the toolhead back into the AMS. Filament or spool may be stuck.
fix_steps: Check whether the spool is tangled or has filament crossed over itself.
Confirm the filament path in the PTFE tubes is clear and unobstructed.
Manually release any tangle on the spool and try the unload operation again.
If filament is jammed in the buffer or hub, open the AMS and clear the jam before retrying.

errors.name: AMS firmware mismatch
errors.description: The firmware of the AMS does not match the printer firmware. An update is required.
fix_steps: Go to the Firmware page in the printer settings or in Bambu Studio.
Update the AMS firmware to the version matching the current printer firmware.
After updating, restart both the printer and AMS.
Do not start a multi-color print until firmware versions are synchronized.

errors.name: First layer inspection not supported for this print
errors.description: First layer inspection is not supported for the current print job configuration.
fix_steps: This is informational. The print can usually continue normally.
First layer inspection may be unsupported for certain model types or file configurations.
In Bambu Studio, enable first layer inspection only for supported models.
For unattended printing, manually inspect the first layer before walking away.

errors.name: First layer inspection timed out
errors.description: First layer inspection timed out. Results may be inaccurate.
fix_steps: Manually inspect the first layer on the build plate before leaving the print unattended.
Check that the internal camera view is not obstructed by filament strands or debris.
Verify your network connection is stable if using remote monitoring.
Consider cleaning the camera lens with a dry cloth if inspections consistently time out.

errors.name: Bed leveling failed: Z-calibration or mesh probing error
errors.description: Bed leveling failed during Z-calibration or mesh probing.
fix_steps: Remove the build plate and clean any filament blobs or debris from the nozzle tip and bed surface.
Reinstall the plate flat and fully seated on all corners.
Run a full Calibration from the printer menu before the next print.
If probing consistently fails in the same spot, inspect the plate for warping.
Replace a warped plate; slight warps can sometimes be corrected by resetting in Bambu Studio.

errors.name: Flow calibration / pressure advance calibration failed
errors.description: Flow calibration or pressure advance (PA) calibration failed to complete successfully.
fix_steps: Verify the nozzle is not partially clogged; perform a cold pull or swap to a fresh hotend.
Check that the filament is dry and not extremely soft, brittle, or degraded.
Re-run flow calibration with default speeds; avoid touching the printer during the test.
If it continues to fail, use a known-good filament profile manually rather than relying on auto-calibration for that material.

errors.name: Filament runout at extruder
errors.description: Filament runout detected at the extruder sensor (not AMS-side).
fix_steps: Check that filament is still present on the spool or in the AMS slot feeding the toolhead.
If the spool is empty, load a new spool and cut a clean, sharp tip.
Feed filament to the extruder until grabbed, then use the Load function and resume.
If the code appears with a full spool, inspect the runout sensor area for debris or a stuck lever arm.

errors.name: Extruder motor overload or step loss
errors.description: Extruder motor overload or step loss detected. Possible clog or excessive resistance in the filament path.
fix_steps: Listen for clicking or grinding from the extruder during printing; stop if heard.
Heat the nozzle and unload filament; check the tip for a thick plug or burnt material.
Perform a cold pull or replace the nozzle or hotend if manual resistance is high.
After clearing, reduce print speed and flow rate for very viscous filaments.
Check the extruder gear for accumulated filament dust and clean if needed.

errors.name: Axis homing failed
errors.description: Axis homing failed. X, Y, or Z endstop error or obstruction preventing homing.
fix_steps: Power off the printer and gently move the toolhead and bed by hand to feel for binding or obstruction.
Look for stray parts, clips, failed prints, or supports blocking motion on any axis.
Turn power back on and run a homing cycle with the door open to watch movement.
Check belt tension on X and Y axes.
If an axis consistently fails to home, inspect the endstop sensor and contact support if the motor or sensor appears damaged.

errors.name: Y-axis belt or motor stall detected
errors.description: Y-axis belt or motor stall detected during printing.
fix_steps: Inspect the Y-axis rails and rods for dirt or hardened grease; wipe with a lint-free cloth.
Verify the bed moves smoothly front to back without scraping the side panels or cables.
Check belt tension; it should be firm but not overly tight or loose.
In Bambu Studio, reduce acceleration and speed if stalls are intermittent.
Contact support if the belt looks worn or the motor exhibits unusual noise.
